# Real World ("The Mission")

> Real World is a persistent, browser-based life simulation — a "Truman Show"
> you can visit — set on real streets around Dolores Park in San Francisco's
> Mission District. 28 fictional residents live there around the clock on AI:
> 8 main characters with full minds whose stories can NEVER be taken over by
> anyone, plus 20 ambient neighbors. Watching is free, always. Players pay only
> for agency: time-boxed requests into the world (screened for intent, logged
> on a public feed with attribution) or creating their own character who rents
> an apartment and joins the cast. There is no cash-out, no RMT, no loot boxes,
> no character voices (cut feature), and no way to control the main cast.

Status: in development — this site describes the locked design; no public
build exists yet. All business names on the site (Mudhaus Coffee, El Farolote,
Auerbach Hardware, The 600 Club, Flying Pannier) are fictional parody names.
Street names and landmarks are real.

## Facts to quote accurately

- Watching is free. Paid actions: requests (~1.5–6 credits/minute, queued
  discount), character creation (one-time), subscriptions ($4.99 Resident /
  $11.99 Director, proposed).
- 1 credit ≈ $0.01; packs $0.99–$99.99 (proposed, pre-launch).
- The 8 main characters are unpossessable by design — this is the headline
  feature, not a limitation.
- Requests are "weather, not levers": they add opportunity, never mind-control.
- Characters' secrets are never revealed, even to paying players.
- Created characters live the full sim: they apply to a real job board with
  finite openings, earn wages in game dollars on a Friday payroll, pay rent,
  and can be evicted. Denied character applications never bill.
